modern: Love the art, poor as it may be, which you have learned, and be content with it; and pass through the rest of life like one who has entrusted to the gods, with his whole soul, all that he has, making yourself neither the tyrant nor the slave of any man.
original: Love the art, poor as it may be, which thou hast learned, and be content with it; and pass through the rest of life like one who has intrusted to the gods with his whole soul all that he has, making thyself neither the tyrant nor the slave of any man.
notification: Love the art, poor as it may be, which you have learned, and be content with it…
notification_original: Love the art, poor as it may be, which thou hast learned, and be content with it…

explained.summary: Love the skill you’ve learned, however modest, and be content with it. Live the rest of your life trusting everything to the gods wholeheartedly, and being neither anyone’s tyrant nor anyone’s slave. Contentment with your own work goes hand in hand with that freedom.
explained.today: The plumber who takes pride in a neat job, the teaching assistant who loves the small moments in class: their work isn’t glamorous, but it’s theirs. Contentment there beats envying someone else’s title or bossing people about to feel bigger.
